recipe.title: Baked Plum & Quark Pots with Cinnamon and Walnuts
recipe.description: Warm cinnamon-baked plums spooned over cool creamy quark with crunchy walnuts, creating a simple sweet-tart evening snack with strong temperature and texture contrast.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Use 320 g; retail pot size may vary.
ingredients.notes: Use a thick plain quark without added sugar.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Choose ripe but still firm fruit so the pieces soften without collapsing.
ingredients.notes: Whole plums do not scale perfectly for every serving quantity; round sensibly when scaling.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Use 16 g; retail pack size may vary.
ingredients.notes: Use fresh walnuts with no bitter or stale flavour.
The small amount of honey helps the plum juices glaze during baking without making the snack excessively sweet.

equipment.notes: Used as a compact oven to bake the plums quickly.
Use a shallow heatproof dish that fits comfortably inside the air fryer and retains the plum juices.
Used to portion the quark and walnuts.

equipment.display_name: 2 serving pots or lidded snack containers
equipment.notes: Use lidded pots if preparing the snack ahead.

mise_en_place.instruction: Halve the washed plums around the stones, twist the halves apart and discard the stones. Cut each half into 3 wedges, retaining the edible skins.
mise_en_place.endpoint: The plums are divided into 12 similarly sized wedges that will soften evenly during baking.

mise_en_place.instruction: Weigh 16 g walnuts and roughly chop them into coarse pieces approximately 5-8 mm across.
mise_en_place.endpoint: The walnuts remain in substantial crunchy pieces rather than fine crumbs.

procedure.title: Season the plums
procedure.instruction: Place the plum wedges in the air-fryer-safe dish. Add 1 tsp runny honey and 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon, then turn the wedges gently until their cut surfaces are lightly coated.
procedure.endpoint: The plum wedges are evenly cinnamon-coated with a thin sheen of honey and remain intact.

corrective_actions.condition: The plums are extremely ripe and begin breaking apart during mixing.
corrective_actions.action: Stop turning them and use a spoon to distribute the honey and cinnamon over their surfaces instead.

procedure.title: Bake until tender and glossy
procedure.instruction: Place the dish in the air fryer and bake at 190°C for approximately 9-11 minutes. Check once after approximately 8 minutes and gently turn the wedges if one side is colouring significantly faster.
procedure.endpoint: The plums are fully tender when pierced with the tip of a knife, their edges are beginning to caramelise, and the released juices have become glossy and lightly syrupy rather than watery.

corrective_actions.condition: The plum edges darken before the flesh becomes tender.
corrective_actions.action: Reduce the air-fryer temperature to 175°C and continue until the wedges yield easily to the knife.

corrective_actions.condition: The plums are tender but the juices remain very watery.
corrective_actions.action: Continue baking for 1-2 minutes, checking every minute, until the juices visibly thicken.

procedure.title: Portion the quark
procedure.instruction: While the plums bake, divide the 320 g quark evenly between the two serving pots, giving approximately 160 g per serving. Keep refrigerated if the plums still have several minutes to cook.
procedure.endpoint: Each pot contains an even portion of cold, thick quark.

procedure.title: Rest the baked plums briefly
procedure.instruction: Remove the baked plums from the air fryer and leave them in their dish for approximately 2 minutes so the bubbling juices settle and the fruit cools slightly before meeting the cold quark.
procedure.endpoint: The plums remain distinctly warm but are no longer aggressively steaming, and the juices coat the fruit rather than running like water.

procedure.title: Finish the pots
procedure.instruction: Divide the warm baked plum wedges evenly over the cold quark, spooning the cinnamon-plum juices over the fruit. Scatter half of the chopped walnuts over each pot immediately before serving.
procedure.endpoint: Each serving has distinct layers of cool creamy quark, warm glossy plum and crisp walnuts, with no excessive liquid pooling in the bottom.

corrective_actions.condition: The plum dish contains more thin liquid than is desirable for the pots.
corrective_actions.action: Spoon the fruit onto the quark first and add only enough of the juices to lightly glaze the surface.

plating.instruction: Serve immediately for the strongest contrast between cold quark, warm cinnamon-baked plum and crunchy walnuts. Stir lightly while eating rather than fully mixing the pot before serving.

storage.storage_instructions: For make-ahead use, cool the baked plums completely before refrigerating them separately from the quark. Store both in sealed containers for up to 2 days. Keep the walnuts dry and separate until immediately before eating. The snack may be served chilled if prepared ahead; warming the plums is optional rather than necessary.
reheating_methods: Air fryer: if warm plums are preferred, place only the baked plum portion in a suitable heatproof dish and heat at approximately 160°C for 2-3 minutes until gently warmed, then spoon over cold quark.
Hob: place only the baked plums and their juices in a small saucepan over low heat for 1-2 minutes until gently warmed.

either_retailer: Low-fat plain quark — 1 pot; use 320 g.
Walnut halves or pieces — 1 pack; use 16 g.

restaurant_quality_features: Baking concentrates the plum flavour and creates lightly caramelised edges.
Cinnamon and a small amount of honey form a glossy natural fruit sauce without requiring a separate topping.
Warm fruit against cold quark provides useful temperature contrast.
Coarsely chopped walnuts provide a distinct crunchy counterpoint to the soft fruit and creamy dairy.
The restrained ingredient list keeps the snack practical while preserving strong flavour and texture contrast.
nutrition_notes: Evening snacks have no minimum protein requirement.
Quark provides substantial protein and calcium.
Plums provide fruit, fibre and micronutrients.
Walnuts contribute predominantly unsaturated fats and useful omega-3 alpha-linolenic acid.
Nutrition values are estimates and will vary slightly with plum size and the exact quark product used.
critical_success_factors: Use ripe but still structurally firm plums so they become tender without collapsing into purée.
Bake until the plum juices become glossy rather than removing the fruit while the juices are still watery.
Allow the plums a short rest before spooning them over cold quark.
Keep the walnuts separate until serving so they remain crisp.
Preserve the warm-fruit and cold-quark contrast when serving immediately.
